root_cause.text: The driver used an unconditional WARN_ON(1) placeholder instead of proper input validation to handle the unimplemented NPU_OP_RESIZE command, allowing userspace to trigger kernel warnings that can be escalated to panics via the panic_on_warn sysctl.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces `WARN_ON(1); // TODO` with `return -EINVAL;` in the NPU_OP_RESIZE case handler within ethosu_gem_cmdstream_copy_and_validate(). The CVE description explicitly states that the WARN_ON(1) "fires unconditionally whenever userspace submits this command via DRM_IOCTL_ETHOSU_GEM_CREATE, causing unbounded kernel log spam" and that "if panic_on_warn is set the kernel panics, giving any unprivileged user with access to the DRM device a trivial denial-of-service primitive."

intent_record.how: Previously, encountering NPU_OP_RESIZE would log a warning but continue execution (break to next iteration). Now it immediately returns an error code (-EINVAL), causing the function to fail and propagate the error up the call stack instead of silently proceeding.

bic_trace_step.reason:
The vulnerable construct is clearly present in the code. At line 447-449 in the `ethosu_gem_cmdstream_copy_and_validate` function, there is an unconditional `WARN_ON(1)` placeholder for the `NPU_OP_RESIZE` command case:

c
case NPU_OP_RESIZE: // U85 only
    WARN_ON(1); // TODO
    break;


This is the exact vulnerability described in the root cause: an unconditional WARN_ON(1) placeholder instead of proper input validation. The comment "// TODO" confirms this is unimplemented. When userspace sends a command stream with the NPU_OP_RESIZE operation, this code path will be triggered, causing a kernel warning that can be escalated to a panic if the `panic_on_warn` sysctl is enabled. The function does not return an error code or perform any validation for this operation - it simply warns and continues. This allows userspace to trigger kernel warnings without proper bounds checking or validation of the resize operation parameters, which is the security issue.
